provenance.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
affiliations: Google (Vedant Misra; affiliation at the time of the work)
provenance.abstract: Neural networks can memorize small algorithmic datasets yet generalize only after many further optimization steps (grokking). On finite binary-operation tables, the authors demonstrate delayed generalization, show that smaller training sets require rapidly increasing optimization, compare optimizers and regularizers (with weight decay especially improving data efficiency), and visualize learned symbol embeddings using a small decoder-only Transformer.
key_claims: A small decoder-only Transformer can first memorize a small algorithmic training set and later generalize to held-out equations after prolonged optimization.
For S5 product, decreasing the training fraction near 25-30% sharply increases the median updates needed to reach 99% validation accuracy.
Weight decay substantially improves data efficiency on the studied binary-operation tasks.
The learned output-layer symbol embeddings can reflect structure of modular arithmetic and S5.
In modular division mod 97 with 50% training data, near-perfect training accuracy precedes near-perfect validation performance by orders of magnitude in updates.

evaluation_protocol.compute: The paper reports optimization-update budgets (1e5, 5e5, and 1e6) but not a hardware type or wall-clock compute budget.
special_conditions: The default paper configuration uses AdamW, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 1, betas (0.9,0.98), 10-update linear warmup, and batch size 512 or half the training set, whichever is smaller.
Section 3.1 uses Adam without weight decay and a 1e6-update budget; Section 3.1.1 uses a 5e5-update budget and seven seeds.
Other dataset-size and ablation runs use three seeds; the complete operation list is in Appendix A.1.1.
The paper reports a 40-50% increase in median generalization time for a 1 percentage-point data reduction around 25-30% training data on S5 product.
The reproduction manifest makes explicit choices for unspecified data-fraction grids, the Appendix A.4 operation, visualization checkpoints, and sharpness checkpoint step.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Use the released authors' S5 product convention (x*y)[i]=y[x[i]]) for permutation arrays and the same product operation consistently in S5 variants.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The public OpenAI grok data.py computes the product as c=b[a]; the paper does not specify an array-composition convention.
alternatives: Use the opposite but isomorphic permutation-composition convention.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Train on the answer token only, with an EOS prefix in the input; do not add a loss term for a trailing EOS token.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The paper says loss and accuracy are calculated only on the answer part; the official implementation wraps EOS tokens and its right-side slice also includes the trailing EOS.
alternatives: Match the official implementation's loss over answer plus trailing EOS.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Use 5-percentage-point grids from 5% to 95% for the variety and ablation curves, with denser S5 time-to-generalization samples around 25-32%.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The article describes the curve trends and calls out 25-30%, but does not list every fraction used.
alternatives: Recover the original unreported fraction list from author-run artifacts, if available.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Use modular addition for the Appendix A.4 outlier study because the paper does not identify the operation in the text or caption.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Appendix A.4 names a modified binary operation but omits its identity; the configuration records this choice explicitly.
alternatives: Run the same k-outlier grid on S5 product or modular division.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Use 50% train fraction and seed 0 for representative Figure 3 embedding visualizations; use 70% train fraction, 100k updates, and seeds 0-19 for the Figure 7 sharpness suite.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The exact visualization checkpoint is not specified; the authors' compute_sharpness script lists S5 checkpoints with train fraction T-70 and seed IDs 0-19, while the paper specifies only a fixed step count with about half the models grokked.
alternatives: Select a different fixed step count or a fraction that empirically yields approximately half grokked models.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Use t-SNE with PCA initialization, perplexity 30, and random state 0 for deterministic embedding plots.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The paper identifies t-SNE but does not report its numerical hyperparameters.
alternatives: Use different t-SNE initialization, perplexity, or random seed.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Export modular-addition truth table as the Figure 5-style example rather than claiming an exact reconstruction of the paper's pictured table.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Appendix A.2 says the figure is one of the operation tables but does not identify the operation or symbol-to-letter assignment in the text.
alternatives: Select another operation and/or reproduce the exact pictured symbol assignment if it can be recovered.

ambiguities.description: The paper describes an outlier-augmented binary operation but does not identify which operation is used in the extracted text/caption.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Use modular addition and disclose the choice.

ambiguities.description: The article does not state how permutations are encoded as arrays or which composition convention is used.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Use the authors' released code convention c=b[a] for the product and apply it consistently to the S5 operations.
alternatives: Use the opposite convention; it is isomorphic but changes labels and representation.

ambiguities.description: The prose says answer-only loss, while the released source's EOS-wrapped shifted target slice includes the answer and trailing EOS.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Use answer-token-only loss to match the paper's prose; log this as a deviation from the source implementation detail.
alternatives: Train on the answer plus trailing EOS as in the released source.

ambiguities.description: Not all data fractions, visualization checkpoints, and the fixed sharpness-evaluation step are specified in the paper text.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Use the explicit grids and checkpoint choices in configs/experiment_suite.json; preserve the paper's reported budgets and seed counts where stated.
alternatives: Recover and use private/original experiment logs if they become available.

ambiguities.description: The paper identifies the pictured example as a binary operation table, but the text does not specify which operation or symbol-to-letter assignment is depicted.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Export a modular-addition truth table as a Figure-5-style artifact and do not claim it is the exact pictured table.
alternatives: Recover the exact operation and symbol permutation from the figure or author data.
